In America Is in the Heart, the narrator asks if there is a Moses of the Philippines and is told “Yes, … his name is [this author].” This Filipine national hero wrote the novels El filibusterismo and Noli Me Tángere.

bonuses.leadin: Two values of this quantity, each for a different material, appear in Snell’s law. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this “index,” the ratio of the speed of light in a given material divided by the speed of light in a vacuum.
Materials with this property have different refractive indices along separate axes. The Michel–Levy chart allows one to identify minerals based on their degree of this property.
This device uses a birefringent material to convert between linear and circular polarization by introducing a 90-degree phase shift between the two perpendicularly polarized components.

bonuses.leadin: A 2023 Jamey Jesperson article that examines “transfeminine life and death in New Spain” is titled “Transmisogyny in the Colonial [one of these places].” For 10 points each:
parts: Name these locations, which collect primary source documents for historians. An online “Internet” one of these places hosts the Wayback Machine.

Jesperson heavily cites Jules Gill-Peterson, whose best-known book documents trans people with this status in 20th-century America. Philippe Ariès’s (“ar-YESʼs”) book Centuries of [this status] argues that this status is a modern invention.

Jesperson argues that the first record of trans Indigenous people in the archive is the execution of “young men in women’s apparel” by this conquistador, the first European to view the eastern shore of the Pacific Ocean.

bonuses.leadin: In a play, a character is asked to put on a suit and pretend to walk through a gate his brother works at after receiving one of these objects. For 10 points each:
parts: What sorts of objects are exchanged between Zachariah and Ethel Lange? Collections of these objects make up epistolary novels.
Tensions develop between Zachariah and his white-passing brother Morris as they play role-playing games to prepare for Ethel’s visit in a play by this author.

A man in another Fugard play describes stealing Robert Zwelinzima’s identity in a letter to his wife, which he dictates to the audience in front of a character who has this profession. Styles leaves his Ford factory job to take on this profession.

bonuses.leadin: English speakers can use the mnemonic “it’s no sin to [have this trait]” to distinguish between the Hebrew letters “sin” and “shin.” For 10 points each:
parts: What stigmatized trait is indicated by the Latin word sinistra?
On the other hand, this English-language word for one’s fine motor skills comes from Latin for “right.” A Dungeons & Dragons statistic with this name measures a character’s agility.

The Russian nickname Levsha, or “Lefty,” unusually denotes skill thanks to a Nikolai Leskov story in which a craftsman makes a steel one of these animals. These animals would pull tiny carts and fight with tiny swords in a popular 19th-century entertainment.

bonuses.leadin: A Frans de Waal book about this order and “philosophers” examines morality through an evolutionary lens. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this taxonomic order to which most philosophers belong, which is also studied in de Waal’s research on apes.

Primates and Philosophers includes responses from Peter Singer and this Harvard philosopher who argued for animal rights using Kantian ethics in her book Fellow Creatures. This thinker wrote The Sources of Normativity.

Much of de Waal’s work is critical of “veneer theory,” which de Waal traced back to this earlier thinker. In one book, this thinker claimed that the agreement of men is “is by covenant only” while defining a commonwealth.

bonuses.leadin: In a “Great Rite,” a priestess of this religion symbolically plunges an athame (“ATH-uh-may”) knife into a cup. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this British neopagan religion whose festivals follow a “Sacred Wheel.” Gerald Gardner’s book “Witchcraft Today” influenced this primarily Celtic and Germanic-influenced religion.
Some Wiccans partake in a “dumb supper” ritual on this holiday in which they eat a silent meal to honor the dead. A wood straw cross called a parshell is hung outside homes on this holiday.
Alongside Wiccans, adherents of this belief system believe in an afterlife called Summerland. Helena Blavatsky and Henry Olcott founded this 19th-century Indian-inspired belief system.

bonuses.leadin: This actor insists on hearing her husband’s African-American coworker sing during a painfully awkward scene in which she serves a breakfast of spaghetti. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this actor who used muttering tics in a 1974 film that ends with her helping clean a trashed dining room with Peter Falk.
Gena Rowlands and Peter Falk played a troubled couple in A Woman Under the Influence, a landmark film in this category. This term refers to a film produced outside a major studio.

The real-life Peter Falk reveals that he was once an immortal being in this film, which features a performance by Nick Cave in a Berlin bar. This Wim Wenders film uses black-and-white shots to show the perspective of angels.

bonuses.leadin: Dr. Harvey Wiley’s unethical experiments on the volunteer “poison squad” led to the passage of this bill. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this Square Deal act initially enforced by the Bureau of Chemistry. Robert La Follette criticized one industry’s “villainous devices” to support this act, which was also supported by a 1906 novel that “hit the public in the stomach.”

The Pure Food and Drug Act and the Federal Meat Inspection Act were passed as part of this president’s Square Deal. This president formed the Progressive Party after claiming he felt as strong as a “bull moose.”

This Supreme Court Justice dissented in US v. Johnson, arguing that false claims about a drug’s efficacy are prohibited under the Pure Food and Drug Act. This later chief justice unsuccessfully ran for President on an anti-neutrality platform.

bonuses.leadin: The U12-dependent “minor” type of these structures is flanked by AU-AC sites instead of the usual GU-AG sites. For 10 points each:
parts: Name these structures that are excised by a ribonucleoprotein complex composed of snRNAs like U2. An alternative form of that process can produce protein isoforms.
RNA splicing is largely absent from these single-celled organisms, whose lack of membrane-bound organelles differentiates them from eukaryotes.

Introns are represented as arrow-studded thin lines between horizontal bars in these visualization tools. Popular examples of this type of software include IGV, Ensembl, and a namesake one hosted by UCSC.

bonuses.leadin: Two popular pieces in the classical repertoire of this instrument are “Ambush from Ten Sides” and “Flowery Moonlit River in Spring,” which highlight the differences in its “martial” and “civil,” or wu and wen styles. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this string instrument played by virtuoso Wú Mán, who trained in its Pudong style. Pieces for this instrument were compiled and published in the 19th-century Hua collection.

Wú Mán has featured on albums such as Beyond the Horizon and A Playlist without Borders with this ensemble. In 2020, Rhiannon Giddens took over as Artistic Director of this ensemble from its founder, Yo-Yo Ma.
Wú and Ma performed at the White House in 1999 to premiere a Bright Sheng work of “three songs” for pípá and this instrument played by Yo-Yo Ma.

bonuses.leadin: Shared similes such as those comparing both Gilgamesh and this hero to lions mourning their cubs led Michael Clarke to argue that the Iliad may have drawn from Mesopotamian sources. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this Greek hero, the central character of the Iliad, who is compared to a lion while mourning the death of Patroclus.
Scholars agree that this Greek mythological figure was likely derived from the Mesopotamian god Tammuz. This man was turned into an anemone flower after his death.
As theorized by Salomon Reinach, the worship of Tammuz as the “all-great Tammuz” may have inadvertently led to the sailor Thamus spreading a rumor about this Greek god.

bonuses.leadin: This molecule composed of excited atoms was the first observed Rydberg molecule. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this molecule, whose fully filled sigma-1s and sigma-star-1s molecular orbitals with no other MOs give it a bond order of zero. This molecule’s bond length of 5200 picometers makes it the largest diatomic molecule.

Despite having zero bond order in MO theory, dihelium is held together very weakly by these intermolecular forces named for a Dutch physicist. London dispersion and dipole-dipole interactions contribute to these forces.

Dihelium molecules have been observed to fit inside these other compounds in a host-guest relationship. These allotropes are denoted with the formula C-sub-x, where x is the number of atoms within the compound.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about American computers during World War II, for 10 points each.
parts: The SIGSALY project performed this task with transmitted sound. This task was assisted by Navajo “talkers” and performed by the German Enigma machine cracked by Alan Turing.

During the war, this scientist was contracted to create a differential analyzer for missile trajectories. This man wrote about “Science: The Endless Frontier” while heading the Office of Scientific Research and Development.

The ORACLE computer later developed for nuclear reactors was created at this national laboratory. The Army Corps of Engineers also used this Tennessee facility to enrich uranium for the Manhattan project.

bonuses.leadin: In a story by this author, the act of smashing a clock that produces lifelike biblical images every hour is deemed a finer action than creating the clock itself. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this author of “The Most Incredible Thing.” In another story by this author, Karen’s amputated feet continue to dance while wearing the title “Red Shoes” before she prays to God for mercy and proceeds to heaven.

In another Andersen story, two characters who both have this name feud over horses and money. The “Little” character with this name constantly outwits the “Big” one and eventually drowns him in a river.
Andersen’s stories are often classified as belonging to this folklore genre collected by the Brothers Grimm.

bonuses.leadin: This scientist names a ratio equal to [read slowly] “2 C-sub-4-4 over C-1-1 minus C-2-2,” which quantifies how anisotropic a material is. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this scientist who also developed a namesake diode that allows current to reliably flow backwards once a certain reverse voltage is applied.

Zener and J. Herbert Hollomon created a formula that measures how much this quantity’s rate depends on temperature. The “engineering” form of this value denoted epsilon equals the change in length over the total length.

Zener also developed a model of viscoelastic solids that uses a combination of these devices and dashpots. These devices exhibit a restoring force proportional to their displacement according to Hooke’s law.

bonuses.leadin: William P. Alston wrote an essay titled, “What [this character] Should Have Said” that examines divine-command theory. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this title character of a Platonic dialogue, who is on his way to prosecute his father before another figure asks him whether “the pious [is] loved by the gods because it is pious, or is it pious because it is loved by the gods?”
In his namesake dialogue, Euthyphro is interrogated by this philosopher who names a method of inquiry through repeated questioning.

Original-language term required. Peter Geach (“geech”) criticized Socrates’s assumption that one cannot know instances of a word without providing a definition as potentially “morally harmful,” since it leads to this state often translated as “puzzlement,” common in Platonic dialogues.

bonuses.leadin: In one poem, the speaker likens this person’s words to “shooting stars which fell to Earth as kisses” after calling an heirloom “a spinning world of forests, castles, torchlight, [and] clifftops.” For 10 points each:
parts: Name this person who, in a John Milton poem, is addressed as a “son of Memory” that lies under a “star-ypointing pyramid.”

In “Anne Hathaway,” Carol Ann Duffy likens Hathaway and Shakespeare’s marriage bed to “seas where he would dive for pearls,” potentially alluding to a song which this character sings. This spirit sings “Full Fathom Five.”
In response to the censorship of one of her poems, Duffy wrote “Mrs. Schofield’s GCSE,” in which she references this Shakespeare play about “star-cross’d lovers” with a line about “Tybalt’s death.”

bonuses.leadin: Austria-Hungary influenced the industrialization of the Balkans, including in this modern-day country, whose region of Styria was part of the Habsburg Crown Lands. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this Balkan nation where Ivan Hribar headed modernization efforts after an 1895 earthquake struck in Carniola. This country has its capital at Ljubljana (“lʼyoob-LYAH-na”).

In the 1880s, Austria-Hungary used this city's tramways as testing grounds for trams to be used in Vienna. This city was the site of the Markale (“mar-KAH-leh”) massacres during a 1992 to 1996 siege involving the JNA.
While working in this Austro-Hungarian port, Robert Whitehead developed the self-propelled torpedo. The most important Hungarian shipping company, Adria, operated from this port.

bonuses.leadin: A 2021 post by “vegetablerights” summarizes this aesthetic as “mum, dad… im……. im revisiting brideshead.”For 10 points each:
parts: Name this gloomy Tumblr aesthetic inspired by neo-Gothic institutions like Oxford University and Hogwarts.

This influencer community has helped prolong the dark academia aesthetic by promoting novels like Piranesi and The Atlas Six. Many brick-and-mortar stores now stock tables with novels popular in this TikTok community.
This dark academia novel was disqualified from Hugo consideration in the 2023 Chengdu scandal. A 19th-century Oxford society acquires magic powers through translation in this R. F. Kuang novel.

bonuses.leadin: A US government initiative named for people with this quality includes core, developmental, and research objectives among its 2030 goals. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this quality. The WHO, which monitors and promotes this quality, notes that it is “not merely the absence of disease or infirmity.”

This theory developed by Jo C. Phelan and Bruce G. Link seeks to explain why low socioeconomic status persistently predicts negative health outcomes. It posits that socioeconomic status is a risk factor for numerous diseases.

This ethnic group names a public-health “paradox” in which their health outcomes were better than their average socioeconomic status would suggest, which may be partially explained by the salmon bias.

bonuses.leadin: In a reference to this author, a relative of one of his characters is suggested as a second wife for a potentially impotent man in the story “The Headstrong Historian.” For 10 points each:
parts: Name this author who wrote about Jonathan paying off an officer to return a commandeered bicycle in “A Civil Peace.” A novel by this author opens with the bribery trial of Obi, who tries to marry Clara.
The girl from “The Headstrong Historian” and Obi are both related to Okonkwo, whose downfall after killing his adopted son Ikemefuna is chronicled in this Achebe novel.

The osu Chike remembers a song about being flogged in one of these places in a story by Achebe, who also wrote about Michael Obi’s attempts to close the title “Dead Men’s Path” because it cuts through one of these places.

bonuses.leadin: Over 85 percent of these ecosystems have disappeared over the past 200 years due to overfishing of their namesake species, including C. virginica and O. lurida. For 10 points each:
parts: Name these ecosystems whose namesake organisms can break storms and provide habitats for other benthic organisms. The presence of spat indicates the health of these ecosystems, which centrally form at estuaries.
Spat refers to oyster larvae after they attach to surfaces, including these structures. Oysters and other mollusks like snails or clams form examples of these exoskeleton structures.
Oyster filter feeding promotes primary productivity by reducing this quantity in the surrounding environment. This quantity is often measured using Secchi disks.

bonuses.leadin: A playwright with this surname collaborated with Moss Hart on a play in which Mrs. Kirby implies that her husband talks about Wall Street during sex. For 10 points each:
parts: Give this surname of the playwright of You Can’t Take It With You. A playwright with this surname, who collaborated with Amanda Gronich on Here There Are Blueberries, wrote The Laramie Project.

In George Kaufman’s play The Butter and Egg Man, two men with this profession con the protagonist. Thomas Meehan helped write about Max Bialystock, a member of this title profession, in a musical adaptation of a 1967 film.

George Kaufman collaborated on the musical The Cocoanuts, which was written for these brothers. Kaufman also worked on the musical Animal Crackers for these brothers, who included Groucho, Harpo, and Chico.

bonuses.leadin: These women were often atypically well-educated since they were expected to serve as interesting conversational, as well as sexual, partners, although some historians dispute that they were even sex workers. For 10 points each:
parts: Name these high-ranking ancient Greek courtesans often contrasted with pornai. One of these women, Phryne, was legendarily acquitted of impiety after exposing herself to an Athenian jury.

Aspasia of Miletus, the partner of this politician, is thought to have been a hetaira. This statesman led Athens at the beginning of the Peloponnesian War and delivered a funeral oration recorded by Thucydides.
Unlike other women, hetairai were allowed to participate in these social events. Agathon hosted a notable one of these events that was interrupted by a drunken Alcibiades.

bonuses.leadin: The exhibition New Topographics broke ground by emphasizing the “man-altered” character of this genre in the 20th century. For 10 points each:
parts: The Sierra Club commissioned photographs in what genre by Ansel Adams?

Robert Adams compiled stark photos of tract developments and highway billboards in a 1974 photobook titled for this place. The Carter commissioned a 1985 book of portrait photographs titled for this place by Richard Avedon.

Western “straight” photographers like Ansel Adams rejected pictorialism’s soft focus landscapes by instead using high values of this parameter. Depth of field scales with this ratio of focal length over aperture diameter.

bonuses.leadin: According to Amy Lind, this person has become “a modern icon for feminists remaking the nation in the context of neoliberalism.” For 10 points each:
parts: Name this person who, in an 1828 incident in Bogotá, led a group of mutinous officers in a wild goose chase, allowing her lover to escape out the window.

Manuela Sáenz saved this man from being deposed in the Septembrine Conspiracy, leading him to nickname her “Libertadora del Libertador” in reference to this man’s nickname as the “Liberator” of Spanish America.

After a failed 1815 campaign, Bolívar went into exile on this island, where he wrote a famous letter outlining his vision for the future of Spanish America. Escaped slaves fought two Maroon Wars on this island.

bonuses.leadin: Salem–Spencer sets cannot contain any non-trivial examples of these sequences, which are the subject of Szemerédi's theorem. For 10 points each:
parts: Name these sequences in which the difference between any two consecutive terms is constant, unlike in geometric sequences.
In 2004, Szemerédi's theorem was extended with this result, which states that the sequence of prime numbers contains arbitrarily long arithmetic sequences.

The Green–Tao theorem led to improved results concerning the first Hardy–Littlewood conjecture, which generalizes this conjecture. This conjecture has been verified up to 10-to-the-388342, somewhat larger than the 10-to-the-18 upper bound for Goldbach’s conjecture.

bonuses.leadin: A vision of this object claims that its occupant was made of red quartz or gray quartz. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this object, smaller examples of which are occupied by 24 figures with gold crowns. This object is described in Surah al-Baqarah’s Ayat al-Kursi.
The description of the throne of God made of quartz is found in this last book of the New Testament, which also describes the Seven Seals.

After viewing the Throne of God, Jesus views the sixth of seven angels pouring out their bowl in this body of water. In Revelation, this body of water will dry up and allow “kings from the east” to march unperturbed.

bonuses.leadin: Historians of Dutch Golden Age painting agree: there are too many Jan (“yahn”) van Kessels. For 10 points each:
parts: Jan van Kessel the Elder was famous for his detailed paintings of these things, which he once had spell out his name. Rachel Ruysch drew on her father’s research to accurately depict these things in her still lifes of flowers.

Jan van Kessel the Younger took his talents to Spain, where he made paintings in this genre at the court of Charles II. Hans Holbein made paintings in this genre of Thomas More and Henry VIII for the Tudor court.
“The other” Jan van Kessel made many still lifes depicting products from these events. Anthony van Dyck painted Charles I dismounted during one of these events.
